demo_anchored: Scroll the page or make the window smaller. The panel stays with the button.
demo_disclosure_long: The second paragraph is longer, so the box is taller than a fixed height would allow for. Nothing measures it. The browser animates from zero to whatever height the content needs, and back again when it closes.
lede: Five things a page usually needs script for. Here the stylesheet does the work.
text_anchored: The panel is placed beside its button with `anchor-name`{secondary} and `position-area`{secondary}. When there is no room on that side, `position-try-fallbacks`{secondary} moves it to another. Opening and closing is the `popover`{secondary} attribute.
text_disclosure: A `details`{secondary} element. `interpolate-size`{secondary} lets it animate to the height of whatever is inside, and `::details-content`{secondary} is the part that moves.
text_marker: The options are radio buttons. The highlight is one pseudo-element anchored to the option that matches `:has(:checked)`{secondary}, so it slides when the choice changes.
text_progress: The bar along the top of the window fills as the page scrolls. It is an animation that runs on `scroll()`{secondary} instead of on time.
text_reveal: Each row fades in as it enters the window and out as it leaves. The animation runs on `view()`{secondary}, the row’s own position in the window.
title_anchored: A panel that follows its button
title_disclosure: A box that opens to its own height
title_marker: A highlight that slides to the choice
title_reveal: Rows that fade in on scroll
